recent_posts.title: Renew Your PyCharm License and Support Django
recent_posts.summary: The Django Software Foundation and JetBrains are running a limited-time fundraiser ending May 1. Purchasing or renewing a PyCharm Professional subscription at 30% off results in 100% of qualifying proceeds going to the DSF, which funds Django Fellows, community programs, and events.

recent_posts.title: It's time to redesign djangoproject.com
recent_posts.summary: The Django Software Foundation's Website Working Group has announced a planned redesign of djangoproject.com, driven by user research showing the site doesn't reflect Django's current capabilities or target audience. The redesign is structured in three phases: discovery and groundwork (current phase), design (IA, mockups, component-driven design system), and incremental build. The team is seeking volunteers with UX, user research, visual design, information architecture, and marketing skills, and is also calling for financial support from the community to fund paid contractors for specialized work.

recent_posts.title: DSF member of the month - Rob Hudson
recent_posts.summary: Rob Hudson, creator of django-debug-toolbar (used by over 100,000 developers), is featured as the Django Software Foundation member of the month for April 2026. The interview covers his journey from biochemistry to backend Python engineering, the origin story of django-debug-toolbar (inspired by Symfony and motivated by a DjangoCon 2008 keynote), his recent work introducing Content-Security-Policy support into Django core, and his thoughts on open source maintainership. He also discusses his interest in FastAPI, Pydantic-based validation, Rust-based Python tooling, and shares advice for open source contributors about using AI as a curiosity tool rather than a shortcut.

recent_posts.title: New Technical Governance - request for community feedback
recent_posts.summary: The Django Steering Council is proposing a new technical governance model (DEP 0019) and requesting community feedback. The changes aim to simplify and reduce procedural overhead, making governance easier to enact, understand, and more flexible. The formal voting process was suspended last year, and this proposal brings written governance in line with how the council has been operating. The target adoption date is July 1, 2026, with a phased feedback and approval timeline running through June 2026. Community members can participate via the Django Forum.

recent_posts.title: PyCharm & Django annual fundraiser
recent_posts.summary: The Django Software Foundation and JetBrains have launched their annual 'Buy PyCharm, Support Django' fundraiser, running until May 1. Purchasing PyCharm through the campaign link at a 30% discount results in JetBrains donating an equal amount to the DSF. Funds support Django Fellows, Djangonaut Space, Django Girls, and international community events. Alternative donation methods including GitHub Sponsors and corporate sponsorships are also available.

recent_posts.title: Could you host DjangoCon Europe 2027? Call for organizers
recent_posts.summary: The Django Software Foundation's Events Support Working Group is calling for volunteer organizers to host DjangoCon Europe 2027. Teams interested in hosting can submit an expression of interest form, with final proposals due by June 1st, 2026. The post outlines what's needed in a proposal including venue details, organizing committee, legal entity, dates, and budget. The DSF offers $6,000 in grant funding and support through dedicated working groups. Eligible dates for the event fall between January 4–April 26 or June 3–27, 2027, to avoid conflicts with other Python community events and major holidays.

recent_posts.title: Django security releases issued: 6.0.4, 5.2.13, and 4.2.30
recent_posts.summary: Django has issued security releases 6.0.4, 5.2.13, and 4.2.30 addressing five CVEs. The vulnerabilities include ASGI header spoofing via underscore/hyphen conflation (CVE-2026-3902), privilege abuse in GenericInlineModelAdmin (CVE-2026-4277) and ModelAdmin.list_editable (CVE-2026-4292) via forged POST data, a DoS in MultiPartParser via base64-encoded uploads with excessive whitespace (CVE-2026-33033, severity moderate), and a DoS in ASGI requests via memory upload limit bypass (CVE-2026-33034). All issues are rated low severity except the MultiPartParser DoS which is moderate. Additionally, Django 4.2 has reached end of extended support, and users are urged to upgrade to 5.2 or later.

recent_posts.title: DSF member of the month - Theresa Seyram Agbenyegah
recent_posts.summary: Theresa Seyram Agbenyegah, known as Stancy, is featured as the Django Software Foundation member of the month for March 2026. A backend engineer and community builder from Ghana, she shares her journey from attending a Django Girls workshop to leading PyLadies Ghana and organizing PyCon Africa and PyCon Ghana events. She discusses her favorite Django libraries including DRF, django-allauth, and Celery, and offers advice for those wanting to start DjangoGirls events. Published on International Women's Day, she also speaks to the importance of women's representation in tech.

recent_posts.title: Django security releases issued: 6.0.3, 5.2.12, and 4.2.29
recent_posts.summary: Django has issued security releases for versions 6.0.3, 5.2.12, and 4.2.29, addressing two CVEs. CVE-2026-25673 fixes a potential denial-of-service vulnerability in URLField caused by slow Unicode (NFKC) normalization on Windows via urllib.parse.urlsplit(); the fix avoids normalization entirely in to_python(). CVE-2026-25674 addresses a race condition in multi-threaded environments where temporary umask changes could cause file system objects to be created with unintended permissions; Django now uses os.chmod() after os.mkdir() instead of relying on umask. All users are urged to upgrade immediately.

recent_posts.title: Google Summer of Code 2026 with Django
recent_posts.summary: The Django Software Foundation has been accepted as a mentoring organization for Google Summer of Code 2026, marking Django's 21st consecutive year in the program. The post outlines how prospective applicants should engage with the Django ecosystem — starting early, participating publicly on the Django Forum, and demonstrating genuine understanding of the project. It explicitly warns against submitting AI-generated proposals without personal understanding, copying previous proposals, or treating GSoC as a solo internship. First-time contributors are guided to set up Django locally, explore open tickets, and introduce themselves on the forum before crafting a proposal.

top_posts.title: Django 6.0 release candidate 1 released
top_posts.summary: Django 6.0 release candidate 1 is now available for testing before the final release scheduled for December 3, 2025. This marks the string freeze phase and opens the call for translators to submit translations. Developers are encouraged to test the release candidate and report any bugs to help ensure a stable final release.

top_posts.title: Django 5.1 released
top_posts.summary: Django 5.1 has been released with notable improvements such as the LoginRequiredMiddleware for easier authentication enforcement, enhanced accessibility features, and the addition of the querystring template tag. Users are encouraged to upgrade from Django 5.0, which will only receive security and data loss fixes until April 2025.

top_posts.title: Django 6.0 alpha 1 released
top_posts.summary: Django 6.0 alpha 1 has been released, marking the first stage of the 6.0 release cycle and feature freeze. The alpha version includes modern tools and design improvements detailed in the development release notes. The release schedule targets a beta in about a month, followed by a release candidate. This alpha is not intended for production use but allows developers to test new features and report bugs.

top_posts.title: Django 5.1 alpha 1 released
top_posts.summary: Django 5.1 alpha 1 has been released, bringing a kaleidoscope of improvements. The beta release is scheduled in about a month, and users are encouraged to report bugs to the issue tracker.

top_posts.title: Django Admin Theme Roundup 2025
top_posts.summary: The Django admin interface, while powerful for rapid prototyping, can be enhanced visually with various themes. This roundup covers recently updated themes such as Dracula, Django Daisy, django-jazzmin, django-admin-kubi, django-jet-reboot, django-semantic-admin, Simple UI, Grapelli, django-admin-interface, and Unfold in 2025. Themes vary in their complexity of integration and the range of additional features they offer.
